comments.author: @Doxymeister
comments.text: I loved the footage of the ponies running wild. I began my life with horses on a Shetland pony at around age five, then graduated to bigger mounts. Later in life, I returned to Shetland ponies, breeding for the shows. Their personalities are quite...opinionated and a bit spicey, LOL. When breaking to saddle, I had to borrow my nieces who had riding experience and the ponies were occasionally ready to buck them off for a quick laugh. When I put a smaller child up though, they would be the model of good behavior, being careful of their tiny cargo. Now I'm old and unable to keep horses so I love videos about them, especially Shetland ponies.

comments.author: @ponypeterson5375
comments.text: I live in South Texas where we have a few cold days each year. We heat our old farmhouse with a wood stove and that’s where we gather on those cold (to us!) days…rocking chairs, reading, visiting, and lots of coffee ❤  I very much enjoyed this video. We lived out in the bush in Alaska for 2 years so I definitely can relate to the light and dark. Surprisingly, the light was much harder for me to take than the dark. Finally a local told us to hang black garbage bags at the windows and we were able to get good sleep.

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: What a wonderful story! ❤️ Your description of gathering around the wood stove with rocking chairs, books, and coffee sounds incredibly cozy. And spending two years in the Alaskan wilderness must have given you some unforgettable memories! It's fascinating that the endless daylight was harder for you than the darkness. Sometimes the simplest solutions, like those black garbage bags, make all the difference! Thank you for sharing such a lovely piece of your life with us. Wishing you and your family many more warm, peaceful days in South Texas! ❤️

I live in Unst. I can tell you that this video bears little to no resemblance to Saxa Vord except for a couple of pictures and a drone video. Saxa Vord has ONE dome, not two. Weekly quiz nights? The shop shown is not our shop. They had three to choose from yet created an AI picture instead. 
Bobby's bus shelter is not the UKs most northerly either. There are a few others further north. The Skidbladnir long ship wasn't built by volunteers on Unst. It was built in Norway and sailed across the North sea to Haroldswick. A broken generator is a community event? 
Shame.

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: That's such a wonderful observation! Shetland's deep connection to its Norse heritage really does make it feel like a world of its own. If we had to choose one island with the most distinctive identity, we'd probably say Fair Isle. Despite its tiny population and remote location, it has preserved a remarkable sense of community and its world-famous knitting traditions. There's something truly special about a place where everyone knows each other and traditions are passed down through generations. Foula would be another fascinating choice, especially for its isolation and ancient Norse connections. Thank you for watching and sharing such a thoughtful question! Which island would you most like to visit?
